scenes.tts: A growth cone is the spread fan at the tip of a growing axon. Add brain membranes, and within minutes the fan folds into a thin tip. The protein responsible was purified from chick brain and named collapsin. Today it is called Sema three A, and it works at about ten picomolar. Retinal growth cones did not respond. What does the growth cone use to hear it?

scenes.visual: A teal growth cone fan on an axon; yellow dots (brain membranes) approach and the fan folds into a thin tip; the dots are relabelled collapsin then Sema3A; a dashed question box asks what receives it.

scenes.tts: Sema three A is a secreted semaphorin. Two research groups independently found its receptor. It is called neuropilin, and it binds Sema three A tightly. But look inside the cell. Its tail is only about forty amino acids long, with nothing that looks like an enzyme. A receptor that catches a signal must also pass it on. Where is the wire?

Its tail is only about 40 amino acids long, with nothing that looks like an enzyme. A receptor that catches a signal must also pass it on. Where is the wire?
scenes.visual: Zoom to a membrane bar: blue neuropilin spans it with a stubby tail inside; Sema3A docks on top; a dashed question box below asks where the wire is.
scenes.narration: Sema3A is a secreted semaphorin. Two research groups independently found its receptor. It is called neuropilin, and it binds Sema3A tightly. But look inside the cell. Its tail is only about 40 amino acids long, with nothing that looks like an enzyme. A receptor that catches a signal must also pass it on. Where is the wire?

scenes.tts: The answer was a second protein, plexin. In engineered cells, neither protein alone let Sema three A shrink the cell. Together, they did. And the pair holds Sema three A more tightly than neuropilin alone. Plexins are a large family. Membrane semaphorins bind plexins directly. Most class three semaphorins reach plexins through neuropilin.

scenes.visual: Purple plexin appears beside neuropilin; each alone is tagged no shrinking; they slide together under a bridging Sema3A and the tag changes to the cell shrinks.

scenes.tts: Other work split the jobs. A neuropilin without its tail still supported collapse. A plexin stripped of its inner part blocked Sema three A responses in sensory neurons. So neuropilin catches. Plexin signals.

scenes.visual: On the complex, the neuropilin tail is cut away and a green result appears; reset; the plexin inner part is cut and a red result appears; then the labels catches and signals.
scenes.narration: Other work split the jobs. A neuropilin without its tail still supported collapse. A plexin stripped of its inner part blocked Sema3A responses in sensory neurons. So neuropilin catches. Plexin signals.

scenes.tts: Inside the cell, plexin has a domain that acts as a G A P. A G A P is a protein that speeds G T P hydrolysis, and so switches a small G T Pase off. In the first case studied, plexin B one, the reported target is R Ras; later work points to its relative Rap. Both help hold integrin adhesions to the substrate. Switch it off, and adhesion falls.
scenes.caption: Inside the cell, plexin has a domain that acts as a GAP. A GAP is a protein that speeds GTP hydrolysis, and so switches a small GTPase off. In the first case studied, Plexin-B1, the reported target is R-Ras; later work points to its relative Rap. Both help hold integrin adhesions to the substrate. Switch it off, and adhesion falls.
scenes.visual: The plexin inner part moves up under the membrane and ends in a GAP chip; it blocks an orange R-Ras chip carrying a GTP badge; the badge is lost, R-Ras goes grey (relabelled R-Ras / Rap), and the integrin adhesion chip fades.
scenes.narration: Inside the cell, plexin has a domain that acts as a GAP. A GAP is a protein that speeds GTP hydrolysis, and so switches a small GTPase off. scenes.tts: Plexin signalling also engages Rho family G T Pases and proteins that act on actin and microtubules. The net result is a local loss of actin and adhesion. On one side of a growth cone, that means a turn. Everywhere at once, it means collapse. Keep the split. Neuropilin catches the semaphorin. Plexin sends the signal.
